tasks.short: Inspect vehicles for damage and record findings

steps.what: Inspect vehicles for damage and distinguish observed defects from unresolved concerns
Record inspection findings, damage location and supporting observations for repair planning

tasks.design: Retain physical inspection and direct findings capture in the existing workshop record {OTHER}. No vision diagnosis or automatic damage classification is introduced, and no duplicate transcription baseline is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Damage must be observed and described sufficiently for repair planning.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workshop records can hold findings; digital aircraft logs do not demonstrate faster automotive inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish visible damage from hidden problems and communicate uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: Inspect the real vehicle and judge what requires further investigation.
tasks.altitude: Make inspection findings useful without shortening the inspection.

reach.task: Use recorded findings to scope repair work
reach.learn: Which observations need clarification before planning

evidence.claim: AMOS provides digital aircraft job cards and signatures; this does not establish automotive physical inspection savings.
No new reduction is assigned without a demonstrated duplicate recording step.

assumptions: The technician produces damage observations in s1 and captures location, description and vehicle reference in s2, with all capture time retained.
Service intake supplies existing vehicle identity; uncertainty is resolved within retained task time.
No free structured damage code or inspection result feed is assumed.
Current workshop records suffice; no new system or recurring upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Whether findings are currently transcribed more than once
research_questions: Is there a separate repeated transcription step beyond direct findings capture?

already_counted.description: Inspection and findings capture remain fully counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100 with zero incremental work give zero saving. No physical inspection or unobserved transcription reduction is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review work orders and discuss work with supervisors

steps.what: Review work orders and identify unclear scope, constraints and unresolved repair questions
outputs: understood work scope and clarification questions

steps.what: Discuss work with supervisors and agree scope, priorities and escalation needs
inputs: understood work scope and clarification questions
outputs: agreed work understanding and escalation needs

tasks.design: Keep work-order review in the existing workshop system {OTHER} and retain the supervisor discussion. No generated summary substitutes for reading the actual order or resolving scope questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders can leave ambiguity about symptoms, authority and priorities that requires discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Current work-order access supports this unchanged workflow.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise when the written scope does not fit the vehicle or available capacity.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge ambiguity and agree a practical plan with the supervisor.
tasks.altitude: Reliable shared understanding before work begins.

reach.learn: Which order details prevent repeated clarification

evidence.claim: Digital work-order access alone does not remove technical review or supervisor discussion.

assumptions: Service intake produces the issued work order, and earlier inspection produces any available findings; their unchanged capture is outside this review task.
The technician produces clarification questions in s1; all reading and discussion remain in s1-s2.
No automatic priority, scope code or clean order feed is assumed.
Supervisor time remains unchanged and is excluded from focal savings; no new upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Typical order ambiguities and current supervisor availability
research_questions: Which missing order information repeatedly triggers supervisor discussion?

already_counted.description: Order interpretation and discussion remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new summary system or maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero incremental work and zero saving. Supervisor conversation is not shortened by existing digital access.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Troubleshoot fuel, ignition and emissions systems

steps.what: Review symptoms and vehicle specifications and select appropriate diagnostic tests
Use electronic testing equipment to test fuel, ignition and emissions control systems
Interpret test results, investigate inconsistent readings and determine the next diagnostic or repair action
outputs: supported diagnostic conclusion or further test requirement

tasks.design: Retain technician-led testing with current diagnostic equipment and manufacturer information {OTHER}. Existing electronic readings support diagnosis; no new model infers a fault or acts on vehicle systems.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fault codes and measurements require contextual tests rather than a direct code-to-repair lookup.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic testing already exists in the task baseline.
tasks.still_hard: Reproduce intermittent faults and distinguish a cause from a secondary symptom.
tasks.human_edge: Choose and interpret real tests and recognise when evidence is insufficient.

evidence.claim: Electronic testing does not automatically identify the underlying fault; no diagnostic automation evidence is supplied by this digest.

assumptions: Service intake supplies vehicle identity and symptoms; the technician verifies applicability and selects tests in s1.
The technician produces readings and test conditions through physical testing in s2; all acquisition and interpretation time remains.
Current manufacturer information and electronic equipment are already in the baseline, with no new data feed or upkeep.
Repair execution is outside this diagnostic task; repeated tests remain within retained troubleshooting time.
unknowns: Diagnostic equipment coverage and access to vehicle-specific information
research_questions: Which fault classes require repeated testing before a supported conclusion?

already_counted.description: Test selection, physical testing and interpretation remain in full.

incremental.description: No new diagnostic service or upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and zero incremental work give zero saving. Existing electronic diagnostics earn no new credit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss vehicle problems and repair requirements with customers

steps.what: Confer with customers to obtain descriptions of vehicle problems and clarify circumstances
outputs: clarified customer problem description and priorities

steps.what: Discuss work to be performed and future repair requirements and confirm customer understanding
inputs: clarified customer problem description and priorities
outputs: explained work and future repair needs

tasks.design: Retain the customer conversation, using existing workshop findings {OTHER} when available. No intake bot, generated repair recommendation or automatic customer commitment replaces the technician's clarification and explanation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The customer's description often needs questions, and repair requirements need a clear explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing findings and face-to-face conversation support this unchanged task.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve incomplete symptom descriptions and explain uncertainty and future needs.
tasks.human_edge: Hear what the customer means and check understanding without overstating the diagnosis.
tasks.altitude: Clear shared understanding of the problem and repair discussion.

reach.task: Receive customer questions and work preferences

evidence.claim: Digital repair logs do not demonstrate reduced customer clarification or explanation time.

assumptions: The customer produces the initial problem account; technician elicitation and clarification remain in s1.
Inspection staff or the same technician produce available findings during separate inspection; creating those findings is outside this conversation task.
All explanation and understanding checks remain in s2; this is not a purchase authorisation or repair-release step.
Customer time remains unchanged; no new structured symptom feed, application or upkeep is assumed.
unknowns: Whether the technician or adviser leads the current conversation
research_questions: Which customer descriptions most often require follow-up clarification?

already_counted.description: Problem clarification and repair explanation remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new intake bot or content maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and no incremental work yield zero saving. No customer conversation reduction is supported.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain physical inspection, diagnostic judgement and clear repair conversations.
reach: Explain findings to service advisers and customers
role.ambitious_version: A technician who makes evidence and repair requirements understandable while keeping hands-on judgement accountable.
